checksums.name: global_sum16
checksums.formula_detail: stored u16_le at record+0 = (sum of unsigned bytes at logical offsets 2..103 inclusive) & 0xFFFF. FUN_080388cc accumulates bytes in int; store truncates to u16_le. Includes magic byte at +2. Physical sav bytes obtained by reversing each aligned 8-byte block.

checksums.name: slot_sum16
checksums.formula_detail: Per slot: stored u16_le at slot+0 = (sum of unsigned bytes at slot offsets 2..99 inclusive) & 0xFFFF. Same FUN_080388cc. Empty slot sums to 0x0047 (magic only). Slot EEPROM offsets 104,204,304,404.

io_driver_functions.notes: DMA3 primitive: programs DMA3 src/dst/control (enable bit 0x80000000), waits busy bit 0x8000, saves/restores interrupt global. Used for EEPROM transfers to/from 0x0D000000.

Read one 8-byte EEPROM block: builds read command+address bitstream MSB-first (two leading 1 bits), DMA to 0x0D000000, reads 0x44 halfwords, reconstructs 4 u16 MSB-first into descending slots (origin of per-block byte reversal in .sav).
Write one 8-byte EEPROM block: expands 4 u16 MSB-first, appends address, write opcode bits, DMA addr_bits+0x43 halfwords to 0x0D000000, polls EEPROM ready bit with timer timeout.
Wrapper: FUN_0803c670(block, data, wait=1).
Verify block: read via FUN_0803c5ac and compare 4 u16; returns 0 ok / 0x8000 mismatch.
Write block with up to 3 write+verify (FUN_0803c65c+FUN_0803c7d0) retries.
EEPROM type select: arg 4 selects 512-byte config (block count at config+4, address bits at config+8); 0x40 selects larger EEPROM.
Save-bus init: calls FUN_0803c4e4(4), fixing 512-byte EEPROM geometry. Entry/init path, no traced callers.
Read byte range (offset,length,dest): block conversion, unaligned head/tail handling, up to 8 read+verify attempts per block, returns bool.
Write byte range (offset,length,src): block writes via FUN_0803c828, then full read-back via FUN_08034b90 + memcmp FUN_080446b0, returns bool.
Read wrapper with interrupt/DMA-state save-restore guard. Call site: FUN_08034e98(0,0x1F8,ram_buf,2).
Write wrapper with guard save/restore. Call sites: (0,0x68,buf,2) global, (0x68+slot*100,100,slot,2) slots.
Byte-sum: sum of u8 array in int accumulator; callers truncate to u16_le. Global len 0x66, slot len 0x62, both from record+2.
memcmp (word+byte). Used only for post-write read-back verification.
Load+validate entry: read 504 bytes, check global magic/checksum then per-slot; reinit failures. No traced callers.
Init whole image: zero 0x200 RAM, set global header (+2='G',+4=6,+5=0xFF,+6=0x7F), zero 6x16 entries, flush global + 4 slots.
Init one slot: zero 100 bytes, set +2='G', flush via FUN_08025e74.
Flush global: recompute checksum then FUN_08034eb4(0,0x68,buf,2). (Callgraph lists no callers; text call site in FUN_08025cc4.)
Flush slot: recompute checksum then FUN_08034eb4(0x68+slot*100,100,slot_ptr,2).
Accessor reader: returns ~((global_byte3>>1)&1)&1. Only traced payload reader.

open_questions: Semantics of global byte +4 (init 6, observed 6->1): language, counter, volume, or progress value cannot be distinguished from empty saves; fuzzing target #2 and a populated-save capture are required.
Semantics of global +3 bit1 (only reader FUN_08025f08), +5=0xFF, +6=0x7F, and the six 16-byte global entries at +8..0x67: never populated in samples.
All slot payload bytes (+3..+99 x4 slots): both samples are freshly initialized empty slots; no populated save exists in the workspace to subdivide them.
Numeric RAM mirror base address: buffer proven contiguous (global + slots at +0x68) but base is in unresolved Ghidra literal pointers (_DAT_08025df4 etc.) and no ROM is in the workspace to read them.

Gameplay mutators/flush callers outside init/load: FUN_08025e50/0x08025e74/0x08025dd8 have no direct callers in callgraph.json and 0x47/FUN_080388cc appear nowhere else in 223 functions; likely indirect/jumptable calls or untraced code, unresolved.
Meaning of the constant trailing argument 2 at FUN_08034e98/FUN_08034eb4 call sites (ignored by 3-param decompiled range bodies; likely consumed by unrecovered tail code).
No paired .ss save states exist (states/ empty), so all fuzzing predictions are boot-diff predictions, not yet state-reload observations.
